chapter: Prose: The Night Train at Deoli
trick: Nothing happens in this story, and that is the story. The narrator never learns the girl's name, never gets off the train for good, and never finds out what became of her — Ruskin Bond leaves it unresolved on purpose, so that the reader keeps the mystery the narrator keeps. Any question asking 'why did the author not...' has that as its answer.

video.query: the night train at deoli ruskin bond summary class 12 english

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about The Night Train at Deoli.

items.statement: The narrator was eighteen and travelling to his grandmother's house in Dehra.
items.why: He made the journey every summer during his college vacation, and Deoli was a stop on the way.

items.statement: Deoli was a busy junction where the train halted for a long time.
items.why: It was a small, forlorn station where nobody got down and the train stopped for only about ten minutes.

items.statement: The girl sold baskets on the platform.
items.why: She carried a basket on her head and sold them to passengers — that is how the narrator first spoke to her.

items.statement: On his return journey the narrator found the girl and spoke to her again.
items.why: She was not there, and the stationmaster could tell him nothing useful. He never saw her again.

items.statement: The narrator decides at the end that he will one day get off at Deoli and find her.
items.why: He keeps the intention alive without acting on it, which is what preserves the story's romance and its sadness.

trick: Chekhov sets up a bet about capital punishment and then quietly changes the subject: by the end the question is not which punishment is worse but what fifteen years of books do to a man. The lawyer walks out five hours early and forfeits the two million — he renounces it, and the banker is left ashamed. Remember the direction of the moral, because it is the reverse of what the opening leads you to expect.

trick: The tree is not the subject; memory is. Toru Dutt begins with a botanical description, moves to the children who played beneath it, and ends asking that the tree be blessed against oblivion — so the poem travels from sight to memory to immortality. The creeper 'like a huge python' winding round the trunk is the image examiners ask for by name.

video.query: our casuarina tree toru dutt poem explanation class 12 english

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about Our Casuarina Tree.

items.statement: The creeper round the tree is compared to a huge python.
items.why: 'Like a huge Python, winding round and round' — the poem's most quoted image, and it opens the first stanza.

items.statement: The poem is written in praise of the tree's usefulness as timber.
items.why: The tree matters because of the companions who played beneath it in childhood, most of whom are now dead.

items.statement: Toru Dutt links the tree to trees she saw in France and Italy.
items.why: The memory of the casuarina returns to her in distant lands, which is how a private tree becomes a universal symbol.

items.statement: The poet wishes the tree to be forgotten so that her grief may end.
items.why: The opposite — she consecrates it to the memory of her lost brother and sister and asks that Love defend it from Oblivion's curse.

items.statement: Wordsworth is invoked in the closing lines.
items.why: She borrows the phrase about trees in a 'yew-tree' spirit, placing her tree in the Romantic tradition of nature and memory.
